note: Doc 07 #16 micro-tree, verbatim. He is the saddest character in the game and none of this is played as sad.

options.text: Where do the maps come from?

exchange.speaker: map_seller
exchange.line: From the accounts. There’s dozens of accounts.

exchange.speaker: map_seller
exchange.line: You put them together and a picture comes out.

options.text: Have you ever dug where a map says?
options.say: I’d not dig my own map, sir. That’d be like a man eating his own dinner.
options.repeat: Like a man eating his own dinner, sir.

options.text: I am going to leave now, in a dignified manner.

speaker: map_seller
speakerNote: Who says the replies. Without it DialogueRunner leaves `sayer` null, the renderer cannot find a head to put the words over, and they fall to the top-centre fallback in the wrong colour -- which is exactly what Tyler saw.
gateNote: Doc 07’s ↳ notation: "from_what" is a FOLLOW-UP, offered only once "where_from" has been asked. Without the gate every option is on the list from the first moment, which had the pie woman offering to argue with an answer nobody had given.
exchangeNote: Doc 30 section 5: a reply that would wrap past three lines is split at a rhetorical break. Tyler asked for the break-up to be back-and-forth with Thad rather than the same voice twice, and he is right -- an interjection makes the punchline land, where two consecutive lines from one man is just a paragraph with a pause in it.
